correctness.rationale: For every bounded complete trajectory, variation of constants gives \(z(t)=\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-\alpha(t-u)}x(u)^2\,du\ge0\); equality at one time forces the entire trajectory to be the origin. For every continuous test \(\varphi(z)\), stationarity of an antiderivative gives \(\int\varphi(z)(x^2-\alpha z)\,d\mu=0\). This is exactly the defining relation for \(\mathbb E[x^2\mid z]=\alpha z\). The Borel-set and moment-hierarchy formulations follow by standard conditional-expectation approximation. The packaged checker independently verifies the polynomial generator premises.

value.rationale: The accepted statement is not merely another integrated moment. It disintegrates stationary energy by the natural height coordinate and determines the entire \(x^2\)-weighted height law from the ordinary height marginal. This yields an exact Borel-localized identity and an infinite mixed-moment hierarchy for every compact invariant measure, including periodic and chaotic stationary states. That information is strictly finer than the already covered global balance and is naturally tied to the model's linear height-relaxation equation, making it a reusable structural constraint for invariant-measure and numerical-statistics work.
